analysis:
The supplied units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 5678-6530) only; the PR touches only this documentation file, so no executable code or security control changes. I read the excerpts against the threat model, with focus on TB-007, T-041 and the cluster/prefix-cache areas.

The documented behavior includes cluster GLM image ingress with fail-closed and non-advertised qualification gates. It also covers packed KV precision agreement between ranks. Each rank resolves its own settings and the pair refuses to load on a mismatch (fail-closed). The cluster SSD prefix record encoding is described as bound by directory suffix, sealed header and load agreement. Records of a foreign encoding are refused and deleted, and a changed or undecodable record restores nothing. The documentation also covers batch lane drivers, memory/observation records and manifest pin repair.

The documented repair path fetches a CDN manifest and replaces manifest.json only when the fetched bytes name the same artifact and the worker accepts them. It never writes weight files. That is consistent with T-012/T-027 and the existing pin contract, and it is documentation of existing behavior, not a new control.

The SSD records section describes the cluster prefix tier's at-rest records. It states that encoding is sealed and authenticated and that corrupt records are deleted. It does not claim to relax the T-041 TTL or HMAC-name posture. The cluster-record details live in the retained cache threat. The cluster tier (QwenStagePrefixDiskTier) is not listed in T-041 affected_files, which suggests a threat-model documentation gap, but the excerpts do not show enough to claim a regression. The observation logs are stated to be content-free: size-only, with no tokens, logits or prompt text.

The patch excerpt for this file is truncated (changed ranges include 4592-4608 and others outside the supplied units), so those hunks were not reviewed. Remaining question: whether the cluster SSD prefix tier's TTL, KEK binding and salt scoping match T-041 posture. That is the implementation's responsibility and is not evidenced here.
